prompt: Our ride-hailing dispatch service matches each incoming ride request to the nearest available driver, locking the driver in Redis before pulling them out of the matching pool so two riders can never be handed the same driver. In production, when two ride requests for the same area arrive within milliseconds of each other, both get matched to the SAME driver — the driver's app shows two active trips and one rider is silently dropped — but this never reproduces under single-threaded testing, only under real concurrent load. Here's the actual matching function we run: walk me through what happens when two of these calls race each other, tell me exactly where the concurrency defect is, and describe how you'd fix it.
